problem_text:
A coastal municipality is tasked with developing a nutrient runoff mitigation strategy to curtail total nitrogen discharge from several agricultural drainage points. Initially, no intervention practices are in place.

The baseline characteristics for each drainage point are as follows:
* For Field 1, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.65, and the cultivated area is 84.958.
* For Field 2, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.717, and the cultivated area is 119.242.
* For Field 3, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 0.751, and the cultivated area is 71.062.
* For Field 4, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.381, and the cultivated area is 188.349.
* For Field 5, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.974, and the cultivated area is 200.002.
* For Field 6, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.46, and the cultivated area is 201.898.
* For Field 7, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 2.908, and the cultivated area is 244.742.
* For Field 8, the nutrient leaching coefficient is 1.286, and the cultivated area is 222.619.

To address the discharge, several best management practices (BMPs) are available, each with a specific capture efficiency:
* Implementing Practice1 will intercept 22% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice2 will intercept 37% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice3 will intercept 66% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice4 will intercept 49% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice5 will intercept 49% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice6 will intercept 30% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice7 will intercept 66% of nutrients.
* Implementing Practice8 will intercept 86% of nutrients.

Deploying a practice on a drainage point incurs an implementation cost per unit of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all field–practice pairings is detailed below:
| Field \ Practice | Practice1 | Practice2 | Practice3 | Practice4 | Practice5 | Practice6 | Practice7 | Practice8 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Field 1 | 180.603 | 191.388 | 104.029 | 31.421 | 104.921 | 122.847 | 110.374 | 195.762 |
| Field 2 | 197.508 | 187.446 | 35.077 | 173.555 | 117.992 | 79.428 | 139.759 | 154.918 |
| Field 3 | 191.346 | 156.37 | 13.171 | 22.831 | 59.815 | 17.567 | 21.489 | 159.965 |
| Field 4 | 106.256 | 129.428 | 105.199 | 88.932 | 143.344 | 25.661 | 111.947 | 127.049 |
| Field 5 | 62.719 | 68.882 | 107.148 | 48.608 | 163.531 | 111.914 | 84.239 | 130.516 |
| Field 6 | 168.56 | 139.401 | 22.562 | 142.748 | 148.692 | 170.829 | 21.002 | 26.38 |
| Field 7 | 92.552 | 96.141 | 125.678 | 68.765 | 150.922 | 150.725 | 32.694 | 144.501 |
| Field 8 | 143.285 | 41.128 | 191.073 | 109.371 | 158.768 | 146.945 | 41.723 | 34.117 |

The planning authority must decide which practices to apply to each drainage point (fields may adopt multiple practices concurrently), and a field may also remain partially untreated if required. The objective is to guarantee that the total nutrient discharge is diminished by at least a proportion P = 0.591 of the baseline load, while minimizing the aggregate implementation expenditure.
